action.recommendation: Implement basic structured application logging. Use a logging library (Winston, Pino, structlog) rather than console.log. Log at appropriate levels (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR), include request IDs, and persist logs to a file or log service.

rationale: Without logging, debugging production issues relies on user reports and guesswork. Basic logging is the minimum viable observability.

action.recommendation: Upgrade to structured JSON logging for machine-readable logs. Include: timestamp (ISO 8601), log level, service name, correlation/trace ID, and contextual fields. Ensure log levels are configurable via environment variable.

rationale: Structured logs enable log aggregation, querying, and alerting. Unstructured text logs cannot be reliably parsed at scale.

description: Add metrics and alerting for production systems with structured logging

action.recommendation: Add application metrics and alerting to complement structured logs. Instrument: request rate, error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), and business metrics. Set up alerts for SLO breaches. Use Prometheus, Datadog, or CloudWatch.

rationale: Logs answer 'what happened'; metrics answer 'how is the system performing'. Both are required for production observability.

action.recommendation: Implement distributed tracing and APM for your metrics+alerts system. Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation, configure trace sampling (1-10% in production), correlate traces with logs via trace IDs, and use APM dashboards to identify performance bottlenecks.

rationale: Metrics show that something is wrong; distributed traces show where and why. APM is essential for microservices performance debugging.

description: Create operational dashboards for key metrics

action.recommendation: Create operational dashboards for your key services. Include: SLO status at-a-glance, error rate and latency trends, infrastructure utilisation, and business metrics. Store dashboard definitions as code (Grafana JSON, Terraform) for version control.

rationale: Dashboards make metrics actionable. On-call engineers need at-a-glance views to diagnose incidents rapidly.

description: Link alerts to runbooks for incident response

action.recommendation: Link every production alert to a runbook. Runbooks should: describe the alert's meaning, provide diagnostic steps, document resolution procedures, and include escalation contacts. Review and update runbooks after each incident.

rationale: Alerts without runbooks cause slow incident response. Runbooks reduce MTTR by providing immediate diagnostic guidance.

description: Define and monitor Service Level Objectives

action.recommendation: Define SLOs for all production services. Document: availability target (e.g. 99.9%), latency SLO (p95 < 500ms), error budget policy, and burn rate alerts. Review SLOs quarterly and adjust based on user feedback and business requirements.

rationale: SLOs align engineering and business on reliability targets. Error budgets provide objective criteria for balancing features and reliability.

description: Define log retention and archival policy

action.recommendation: Define a log retention policy aligned with compliance requirements. Standard retention: 90 days hot storage, 1 year cold storage. For regulated industries: GDPR (minimum required for purpose), PCI DSS (1 year), HIPAA (6 years). Implement automated archival and deletion.

rationale: Log retention must balance operational debugging needs, compliance requirements, and storage costs.
